name: OpenSSL base64
tile_line: OpenSSL rates it Low. No attacker path known.
tldr: OpenSSL 4.0 and 4.1 can write past a buffer if a program base64-encodes about 1.6 GB in one call. OpenSSL rates it Low because no attacker path is known, and CISA lowered its score from 9.8 to 5.9. Take the fix with normal updates when it ships.
summary: The bug is in `EVP_EncodeBlock()`. OpenSSL says its own TLS, QUIC and CMS code never encode that much and its command-line tools can't practically be made to; only an app that passes an attacker-controlled length without its own check is exposed. CISA's change came on 20 Nov; Ubuntu rates it Medium.

status.needs: an app that passes an attacker-controlled length of ~1.6 GB to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own check

affected.label: OpenSSL 4.0.0 to 4.0.3, or 4.1.0
affected.text: OpenSSL's CVE record lists only these versions; 3.x and older are not listed. Ubuntu disagrees in one place: it marks the Node.js package on Ubuntu 22.04, which bundles OpenSSL 1.1.1m, as vulnerable. Apps can also bundle their own OpenSSL.

affected.label: Something encodes ~1.6 GB at once
affected.text: A program has to pass more than (INT_MAX / 4) * 3 bytes, about 1.6 GB, to `EVP_EncodeBlock()` in one call. The fix's pull request named the proxy login of `openssl s_client -proxy_pass` as a path, but OpenSSL's CVE record now says the command-line tools can't practically be made to do it, and that TLS, QUIC and CMS never encode buffers that size. The fix changes only the base64 code and the HTTP proxy login code.

affected.label: An attacker controls that data
affected.text: OpenSSL says only an app that takes a length from an attacker and passes it to `EVP_EncodeBlock()` without its own check is exposed, and it knows of no such path. CISA's score, now 5.9 (Medium), still assumes a remote attacker with no login; NVD hasn't scored it itself.

do.label: Update when 4.1.1 / 4.0.4 ship
do.text: OpenSSL's CVE record names 4.1.1 and 4.0.4 as the first fixed versions, and OpenSSL has scheduled those releases for 1 Dec 2026. On 23 Nov the fix was still unmerged, on hold for discussion with changes requested, so check the release notes.

do.label: Only use proxy passwords you set
do.text: If you script `openssl s_client -proxy_pass`, don't let other people supply the password or the environment variable it's read from.

do.label: Cap input in your own code
do.text: If your code calls `EVP_EncodeBlock()` on data from others, reject inputs over (INT_MAX / 4) * 3 bytes. That's the limit OpenSSL's fix enforces.
